Yes: myself, but only because I think that almost everyone is naturally evil. Evil, after all, is merely selfishness, and almost everyone is inherently selfish. If you're reading this post, that probably means that you have more wealth than most people in the world (a computer alone would qualify you), but you prefer to hang onto what money and amenities you have. Why? Because, at a basic level, you'd rather it was your stuff than someone else's stuff, and if so, that makes you evil.

Keep in mind that I don't actually think this is a bad thing. After all, selfishness is actually what created all of this wealth in the first place: if everyone behaved like Jesus and gave away all possessions, no one would have invented cars, airplanes, electricity, and computers. All of our lives are better today because of the actions of those selfish people.

Oxymoronically, evil in moderation is good, and too much good is bad.

Not sure I would define evil as being selfishess. I would probably define evil as actively or purposefully or knowingly seeking or allowing your actions to create a bad situation or experience for others even if there is no personal gain to yourself.

But many (if not most) activities traditionally within the definition of evil are all about personal gain, or at least personal satisfaction: robbery, extortion, rape, even murder in most cases. These are examples of too much evil, wherein the person has seriously harmed others in his quest for personal gain.

On the other hand, as I described, too much good can also be bad, as we'd all starve for lack of resources if everyone refused material possessions. Ultimately, balance is better than either extreme, and I think that an intelligent selfishness, one that recognizes that other people are necessary and helpful, is the best route to a prosperous society for everyone.
